1. (Currently amended) A method of treating a brain, comprising: inserting an elongated device into the brain to create a path; radially expanding the device to create a working channel along the path; and introducing a medical element into the working channel to perform a medical procedure on the brain, __wherein the elongated device is radially contracted and removed from the brain after introducing the medical element__.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the medical element is an instrument.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the medical element is a medicament __introduced into the working channel after radial expansion of the elongated device and before radial contraction and removal of the elongated device from the brain__.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, further comprising creating an opening in a cranium, and inserting the elongated device through the opening.

5. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, further comprising inserting the elongated device between tissue layers within the brain.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, further comprising [[radially contracting and removing the device from the brain]] __wherein radially contracting and removing the elongated device from the brain is performed after introducing the medical element into the working channel__.

7. (Currently amended) A method of treating a tissue, comprising: placing an elongated device into the tissue to create a path; radially expanding the device against the tissue to radially displace the tissue along the path; radially reinforcing the device against the tissue; [[- 16 - 03-0357 (US02) and]] introducing a medical element through the device to perform a medical procedure on the tissue, __wherein the tissue is brain tissue and the elongated device is radially contracted and removed from the tissue after introducing the medical element__.

8. (Currently amended) The method of claim 7, wherein the medical element is an instrument.

9. (Currently amended) The method of claim 7, wherein the medical element is a medicament __introduced through the device after radial reinforcement of the device against the tissue and before radial contraction and removal of the device from the tissue__.

10. (Currently amended) The method of claim 7, further comprising inserting the elongated device between tissue layers.

11. (Currently amended) The method of claim 7, further comprising [[radially contracting and removing the device from the tissue]] __wherein radially contracting and removing the device from the tissue is performed after introducing the medical element through the device__.

12. (Previously presented) The method of claim 7, further comprising treating the tissue in contact with the device with a haemostatic compound to reduce bleeding.

13. (Previously presented) A method of treating a tissue, comprising: placing an elongated device, having a first radially expandable body, surrounded by a stent, which is surrounded by a second radially expandable body, into the tissue to create a path; radially expanding the second expandable body against the tissue to radially displace the tissue along the path; radially expanding the first expandable body to radially expand the stent to reinforce the second expandable body against the tissue; radially contracting and removing the first expandable body to create a working channel through the stent; introducing a medical element through the channel to perform a medical procedure on the tissue; and - 17 - 03-0357 (US02) radially contracting the second expandable body and removing the device from the tissue.

14. (Previously presented) The method of claim 13, wherein the medical element is an instrument.

15. (Previously presented) The method of claim 13, wherein the medical element is a medicament.

16. (Previously presented) The method of claim 13, fu rther comprising inserting the elongated device between tissue layers.

17. (Previously presented) The method of claim 13, fu rther comprising treating the tissue in contact with the device with a haemostatic compound to reduce bleeding.
